answer: An agent economy can resist sybils like a mutual insurer. Identities join a pool whose premium scales with how correlated members' fingerprints are: honest agents pay little, but scripted copies share one risk profile, so every extra fake identity inflates the premium for its operator. Premiums burn each epoch like embers, and history sits in an append-only quartz ledger, so lineage cannot be hidden or repriced later. M fakes cost M fees plus quadratic surcharges, while the ridge between honest and correlated cohorts keeps newcomers cheap - each fake soon costs more than its vote is worth.
